content: The World Health Organization (WHO) is currently in the process of updating its guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations, including transgender individuals. To ensure these guidelines are informed by the lived experiences of transgender people, WHO is conducting anonymized in-depth interviews with a small number of transgender individuals from diverse regions and backgrounds. These interviews aim to document personal stories, values, and preferences to better understand the unique challenges, risks, and needs faced by transgender women and men in relation to HIV and other health issues. Participation in this process begins with a short online survey. By completing the survey, individuals indicate their interest in being interviewed. However, due to the limited number of interviews that can be conducted, not all survey participants will be selected. WHO will choose participants based on a range of experiences and geographic diversity. Those selected will be contacted within one week of completing the survey. The interviews will be conducted via telephone or Skype at a time convenient for the participant and will last approximately one hour. The conversations will be voice-recorded and transcribed electronically. All personal information and responses will remain confidential, and no identifying information will be linked to the interview content. Before the interview begins, participants will be provided with detailed information and asked for their verbal informed consent. Participation in both the survey and the interviews is entirely voluntary. Individuals can decline to participate or withdraw at any time without providing an explanation and without any consequences. Unfortunately, WHO is unable to provide financial compensation for participation, but the organization deeply appreciates the time and effort of those who contribute. The survey includes questions about personal demographics, gender identity, sexual orientation, HIV testing history, HIV status, and experiences with gender-affirming care. These questions are designed to help select a diverse group of participants for the interviews. Participants are not required to answer any questions they are uncomfortable with, and all information provided will be kept strictly confidential. The interviews will explore topics such as personal experiences with HIV prevention and care, barriers and challenges faced, and strategies or solutions that could improve access to services. Participants will also have the opportunity to discuss other health concerns relevant to themselves or the broader transgender community, such as co-morbidities (e.g., tuberculosis, hepatitis, sexually transmitted infections) or mental health and substance use issues. At the conclusion of the interviews, WHO will analyze the collected data and produce a report, which will be shared with participants if they express interest. The report will not include any identifying information. Participants may also be contacted later for follow-up questions if they consent to this. WHO is committed to ensuring that the voices of transgender individuals are heard and that their experiences inform the development of inclusive and effective HIV guidelines. The organization expresses its gratitude to all participants for their valuable contributions to this important work.
